Spatial Variability in and Geostatistical Mapping of Soil Organic Carbon Stocks Under Contrasting Land Uses in Foumbot, Western Cameroon
nodes.venue: Geographies
nodes.abstract: Accurate assessment of soil organic carbon (SOC) distribution is essential for carbon accounting and sustainable land management, yet spatial information remains limited in Central African landscapes. This study evaluated SOC stocks across cropland, grassland, and forest ecosystems in the Foumbot agricultural basin, western Cameroon, at depths of 0–10 and 10–20 cm. Spatial dependence was assessed using semivariograms, while a two-step, land use-based residual interpolation framework was applied. Land use-specific means were used to account for broad land use-related variation, and the resulting residuals were interpolated using Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW). Predictive performance was evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) and compared with direct interpolation and a mean per land use baseline. SOC stocks showed heterogeneity associated with land use, topography, and soil development. The fitted Gaussian semivariogram model described the spatial dependence of SOC stock residuals, with ranges of 167 and 144 m at 0–10 and 10–20 cm, respectively. At 0–10 cm, residual IDW achieved the lowest root mean square error (RMSE; 15.69 t ha−1), closely followed by residual OK (15.82 t ha−1), compared with direct IDW (19.60 t ha−1), direct OK (18.73 t ha−1), and the land use mean baseline (17.76 t ha−1). At 10–20 cm, residual OK performed best (RMSE = 14.28 t ha−1), closely followed by residual IDW (14.44 t ha−1), outperforming direct interpolation and the baseline. Overall, residual-based interpolation reduced prediction errors at both depths, although performance varied by depth and evaluation metric. These findings support its application in SOCS mapping and provide spatial information for targeted carbon management and sustainable soil management in tropical volcanic landscapes.

nodes.name: Root Localization and Cutting Technologies for Mechanized Cabbage Harvesting
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Accurate root localization and precision cutting are essential for mechanized cabbage harvesting, yet reliable linkage between perception and cutting remains difficult under field conditions. This review synthesized recent advances in cabbage root/stem localization, cutting mechanisms, sensor-assisted control, and integrated harvesting systems. The sensing technologies considered include RGB and RGB-D imaging, depth/LiDAR and ultrasonic sensing, and machine-state sensing using IMUs, displacement sensors, and encoders, with particular emphasis on multi-sensor fusion for cutter positioning and adaptive control. Relevant studies were identified through Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases. A structured narrative review approach was adopted, and 55 studies were included in the technical analysis. Unlike previous reviews, focused mainly on harvesting machinery and mechanization, this review emphasizes the perception–localization–cutting–control–performance chain and how sensing results are converted into executable cutting actions. The synthesis shows that strong performance of individual detection or cutting components does not necessarily ensure reliable field harvesting. Major gaps include the limited field validation of closed-loop perception–localization–control–cutting systems, insufficient robustness to occlusion, soil adhesion, plant-posture variation, and uneven terrain, and the lack of standardized end-to-end evaluation protocols. Future research should prioritize multimodal sensing, closed-loop adaptive cutting, perception-to-actuation synchronization, and standardized end-to-end performance metrics.

nodes.name: Robust Waste Image Classification Under Class Imbalance and Visual Variability: Weak-to-Strong Learning with Activation-Guided CutMix
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Automated waste image classification remains challenging because of substantial class imbalance, large intra-class visual variability, and high inter-class visual similarity. We propose a backbone-agnostic weak-to-strong training framework that combines class-balanced focal supervision over weak, strong, and activation-guided mixed views, asymmetric Kullback–Leibler (KL) consistency, and Activation-Guided CutMix. The detached weak-view prediction distribution serves as the reference for aligning the strong-view prediction, while Activation-Guided CutMix centers the replacement region at the highest-response location derived from an intermediate feature map of the base weak view rather than selecting its location randomly. The framework was evaluated on two waste-classification datasets using seven CNN backbones. ConvNeXt-Base achieved 98.88% mean accuracy and 98.44% macro-F1 on the corrected Waste Classification dataset, while ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved 79.20% mean accuracy and 76.73% macro-F1 on WaRP-C. Ablation studies demonstrated performance gains across different backbone architectures, with component-level contributions varying by dataset and backbone. The t-SNE, confusion-matrix, and Grad-CAM analyses provided complementary qualitative evidence of more clearly organized feature distributions, reduced off-diagonal class confusion, and more object-focused activation patterns. Because all auxiliary operations are confined to training, the proposed framework preserves the original single-branch, single-forward-pass inference architecture.

Protocol for measuring the effects of cortical scotoma on visual space perception
nodes.venue: PLOS One
nodes.abstract: We aim to investigate the spatial experience of patients with chronic scotomas caused by lesion to early visual cortex, including primary visual cortex (V1) and adjacent extrastriate visual areas. These experiments are conducted as part of an adversarial collaboration testing contrasting theories of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and two Predictive Processing accounts, Active Inference (AI) and Neurorepresentationalism (NREP). The central question is whether lesions to early visual cortex alter the experienced extent of visual space itself, or instead primarily disrupt stimulus content within an otherwise preserved visual space. To address this, we use paradigms in which patients estimate distances or spatial extents that either span a scotomatous region or fall entirely within intact visual field locations. Psychometric functions relating perceived and physical extent are modeled to estimate shifts in the point of subjective equality (PSE). According to IIT, lesions to early visual cortex, including V1 and occipital extrastriate cortex, should lead to systematic reductions in perceived spatial extent across the scotoma (negative PSE shifts), reflecting a contraction of experienced space. In contrast, Predictive Processing accounts posit that higher-level predictive mechanisms preserve spatial structure despite loss of early input, predicting little or no systematic contraction (with NREP allowing limited context-dependent effects). By quantifying distortions in perceived spatial extent, this protocol aims to distinguish between these competing theoretical predictions.

nodes.name: ProNet: a multimodal MRI brain tumor segmentation and fusion network
nodes.venue: International Conference on Smart Healthcare and Digital Health (SHDH 2026)
nodes.abstract: Multimodal MRI is routinely employed in clinical practice for the diagnosis of brain tumors. Current multimodal fusion methods fail to establish both intra-modal and cross-modal spatial dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose an enhanced nested Transformer architecture—ProNet—which integrates an adaptive multi-level gated aggregation network with a three-dimensional attention reconstruction framework to achieve dynamic multiscale feature selection and precise cross-modal alignment. Experimental results demonstrate that ProNet exhibits robust stability and performance and provides an effective design framework for brain tumor segmentation.

Physics-informed 3D source localization from multichannel seismocardiography
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Signal Processing
nodes.abstract: Seismocardiography (SCG) provides a non-invasive means of monitoring cardiac mechanical activity using wearable accelerometers. However, conventional SCG is typically recorded at a single chest location, limiting the spatial interpretation of the measured vibrations. In this study, we investigate whether multichannel SCG can be used to reconstruct the three-dimensional distribution of cardiac mechanical sources. We developed a physics-informed framework combining an electromechanical finite-element heart model, an attenuating transverse-shear radiation model, and a three-dimensional inverse reconstruction pipeline. Synthetic multichannel SCG signals without valve transients (hence not clinical SCG) were reconstructed using delay-and-sum (DAS), minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR), CLEAN, and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL). Three of the four recovered both position and shape on at least one array geometry. Our sparse Bayesian implementation localized the source but recovered no volume, collapsing onto a few voxels; thus, we report it as an approach we could not successfully adapt. Localization and robustness were evaluated against null controls and under varying noise levels, propagation uncertainties, and array geometries. With the source displaced 2 cm from the array center, a fully enclosing array, as a theoretical upper bound rather than a wearable configuration, recovered the centroid to 0.7–0.9 cm. On a more realizable one-sided array, the estimators separated: sparse deconvolution reached 1.0 cm and the adaptive beamformer 1.7 cm, both inside a 2.0 cm no-information baseline, while conventional delay-and-sum fell well outside it. Shape recovery cleared that baseline on both array geometries and collapsed when inter-channel phase was randomized. Reconstruction remained robust to measurement noise and moderate wave-speed mismatch but was more sensitive to geometric and registration errors. These findings indicate that multichannel seismocardiography, in principle, carries spatial information sufficient to localize cardiac mechanical activity in three dimensions. However, on a one-sided array, that recovery depends on the estimator, and centroid accuracy there requires an unmodeled local shear-speed contrast to stay within roughly 20– 30 % for the most tolerant estimator, and about 10 % for the adaptive one. Shape recovery is the more robust of the two. Forward and inverse models share the same physics, a limit that a structural mismatch test bounds but does not remove.

nodes.name: PMA-SAM2: Prior-Memory Adapted Framework for Automatic Remote Sensing Water Body Extraction
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: SAM2 has great potential for remote sensing water body extraction due to its strong feature representation capability. However, when directly applied to the water body segmentation task, SAM2 still faces several challenges, including domain discrepancy, spectral confusion between water bodies and shadow-like objects, significant intra-class variations, and dependence on manual prompts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the PMA-SAM2, which integrates domain prior injection, prototype memory calibration, and automatic prompt guidance for robust water body extraction. First, a Multi-level Prior Adaptation Module is designed to inject spatial geometric information and texture features into the SAM2 encoder, enabling effective alignment between general visual representations and remote sensing domain features. Then, a Prototype Memory Calibration Module is introduced to dynamically accumulate water feature prototypes under different geographical environments and imaging conditions, improving the model’s robustness to intra-class variations and inter-class spectral ambiguity. Furthermore, an Automatic Prompt Decoder is proposed to transform prototype-retrieved similarity maps into dense prompts, replacing manual prompts and enabling fully automatic water body segmentation. Experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior water body extraction accuracy compared with mainstream segmentation methods, verifying its strong generalization capability and scene adaptability.
